Why don't weight-loss drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy work for everyone?

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (805 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Medications like Ozempic and Wegovy, which contain semaglutide — a GLP‑1 receptor agonist that helps regulate blood sugar, appetite and body weight — have become household names and notable pillars in obesity management for the medical profession.
  • Research has shown GLP-1 medications reduce body weight by an average of 15 percent when used weekly for 68 weeks and combined with lifestyle interventions.
  • These medications don’t work the same way for everyone, however.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Medications like Ozempic and Wegovy, which contain semaglutide — a GLP‑1 receptor agonist that helps regulate blood sugar, appetite and body weight — have become household names and notable pillars in obesity management for the medical profession.

Research has shown GLP-1 medications reduce body weight by an average of 15 percent when used weekly for 68 weeks and combined with lifestyle interventions. This is because semaglutide acts on the brain to increase the feeling of fullness and to decrease appetite.

These medications don’t work the same way for everyone, however. Our multidisciplinary research team at the University of Alberta is working to improve obesity care for people of all ages and to understand why some people respond better to semaglutide than others, and how their weight loss can be maintained over time.

We are investigating the role of energy metabolism as a potentially important piece in a complex puzzle.

According to recent reports, research has shown semaglutide medications to improve quality of life, blood markers such as sugar or cholesterol, strength and overall health. Weight loss is only one measure of how well they work.

We are exploring whether people’s responses to these medications could lie in individual factors such as genetics, metabolism, body composition, lifestyle, microbiota, associated diseases, age and sex.

Energy metabolism may also be an important piece of this puzzle. This is a measure of the total calories consumed (in) and the total calories burned (out). We burn calories all the time: for vital processes like breathing and thinking, physical activities like going to the gym and the everyday act of digesting food.

Industry observers note that when we lose weight, our bodies naturally need less energy. But sometimes, the body goes into an extra “energy-saving mode,” burning even fewer calories than we would expect. This is called metabolic adaptation, or adaptive thermogenesis.

Sources indicate that think of it like a light bulb that automatically dims to save electricity. This is one reason why losing weight can become more difficult over time, sometimes leading to a weight-loss plateau.

In a recent development, changes in body weight and composition (the amount of fat and fat-free mass in our bodies) play an important role in energy metabolism. Both fat and fat-free mass use energy, even when we are resting. As we lose these tissues, our bodies naturally burn fewer calories.

Researchers are still trying to understand whether weight-loss medications influence these processes differently. If we can understand how our bodies use energy during and after weight loss, this could help us develop better strategies for maintaining weight loss over the long term.

In a recent development, we published a recent review of studies investigating the effects of GLP-1 therapies on energy utilization. We found a few studies exploring how semaglutide affects resting energy use, with findings that were neutral or inconclusive.

The question of how semaglutide impacts energy use is an emerging area of study, and remains an open question for exploration.

Industry observers note that at the University of Alberta, we have a gold-standard method to measure energy utilization called a whole-room indirect calorimeter. This is a rare research facility and is similar to a hotel suite that can precisely measure each component of energy use. This room can isolate the effects of changes in someone’s calorie burning at rest, after eating and during exercise.

We are at the moment recruiting research participants with blood sugar regulation concerns, such as insulin resistance or diabetes, who are about to start semaglutide treatment. We will follow their weight loss journey over six months to investigate changes in body weight and composition, and energy utilization using sophisticated approaches.

Understanding how semaglutide influences energy use and body composition, and how these changes interact, could be an key step toward explaining why individuals respond differently to weight-loss treatment.

Recent findings suggest that this will allow us to contribute to more personalized approaches to obesity and Type 2 diabetes management in the future. Having a better understanding of how energy use changes with semaglutide-induced weight loss will also help us to better anticipate potential non-responders (people who do not lose weight) and offer alternative treatments sooner in their health journey.

Importantly, current evidence suggests that if you are taking semaglutide or considering starting treatment, you should make a few lifestyle changes.

Sunna is a an S-Rank Physical Support Agent who specialises in boosting teammates using Attack and Anomaly. Her Ultimate sees her pull out a giant hammer to land heavy damage, and bring teammates into combat using Quick Assist. Sunna’s companion, Bubblegum, can cast Cat's Gaze on enemies, marking them for detonation. Bubblegum can also buff the squad’s attack.

Aria is the other new arrival, the group’s lead vocalist who can shift between two forms, idol projection and construct. Aria is an Ether Anomaly Agent who also deals high burst damage, specifically against enemies who suffer from any Attribute Anomalies.

Sunna and Aria also benefit from the support of the amusingly named Bangboo Biggest Fan, a fan club president who can heal them over time, and boost the squad’s Attack any time two or more Angels of Delusion members are present.

Version 2.6’s S-Rank re-runs are Yixuan (Auric Ink - Rupture), and Yuzuha (Physical - Support), who you can look forward to as part of the banners.

Version 2.6 will also expand Hollow Zero with a upcoming game mode, Operation Matrix. The mode offers themed stages that rotate weekly, each offering new mechanics. You can now also Sweep in Hollow Zero.

Beyond all the celebrations, this update also brings combat kit overhauls to a couple of older S-Rank characters, Lycaon and Harumasa. You can look forward to multiple limited-time events, too, including one where you can earn a new outfit for Pan Yinhu.

Sources indicate that the massive event is naturally going to be themed around Gilded Carrot Day, and it actually starts today. There’s the usual run of login rewards (about 3,300 Polychromes), as well as daily activities. Yet another login event - Gilded Surprise, Wonderful Boo-ns - will be available February 14-23, offering daily draws from a pool of 4 billion Polychrome.

Dota 2 will return to the Riyadh-hosted Esports World Cup in 2027, though dates, format and prize money are still to come. The title has never been won twice, and its prize pool has fallen at every edition so far.

Dota 2’s place at Esports World Cup 2027 was announced without dates, a prize pool, a format or any invited teams. The whole event is listed for July to August 2027.

The 2026 tournament had originally been planned for Riyadh before it was moved to Paris on 20 May 2026.

It has been revealed that the first edition, Riyadh Masters 2024, carried a US$5,000,000 prize pool. In 2025 Team Spirit took US$1,000,000 from a US$3,000,000 pool in a 16-team event. The 2026 tournament ran from 7 to 19 July with 24 teams. That field was eight teams larger than a year earlier.

Industry observers note that the winner still takes a large share. PARIVISION collected US$750,000, or 37.5% of the pool, plus 1,000 Club Championship points. Runners-up BetBoom Team received US$340,000 and 750 points, Liquipedia reported.

In a recent development, those points feed into a larger prize. In 2026 the Club Championship paid US$30 million across the top 24 clubs. The champion club received US$7 million from an overall event prize pool of US$75 million. AG.AL won it with 5,300 points, stopping Team Falcons from winning a third title in a row. For organisations weighing the cost of a Dota 2 roster, that club prize is part of the calculation.

Not every club is staying. Falcons released all five players from the roster that won The International 2025, according to Timesaver.gg.

No club or player has won the event’s Dota 2 title more than once. Each of the three editions went to a different club with a different roster. Gaimin Gladiators beat Team Liquid in the 2024 final. A year later, Team Spirit swept Team Falcons 3-0. As the 2026 champions, PARIVISION now get the first chance to defend the title.

In a recent development, PVISION are your Dota 2 at EWC26 Champions! 👏 pic.twitter.com/34U67Oaj7G.

— Esports World Cup (@EWC_EN) July 20, 2026.

Industry observers note that their rivals arrive in form. Team Spirit went out of the 2026 event before the final. A month later, they won The International 2026 in Shanghai. Yatoro and Collapse became the first players to win three Internationals. Team Yandex finished third at both the 2026 Esports World Cup and The International. After signing ATF, they won PGL Wallachia Season 9 and BLAST SLAM VIII.

The route into the event is taking shape. The organiser’s Road to EWC qualifier programme for 2027 aims to involve 1.8 million players across more than 400 events. Qualifier slots for each game will be revealed later. Counter-Strike 2, already confirmed for both 2027 and 2028, will hold a 32-team event in Riyadh from 20 July to 1 August 2027.

I'm also imagining turning the feeds back on and discovering that everybody is having a massive orgy. Stupid sexy vault dwellers! You'll go forth and multiply when Deep Thought tells you to, and not a second before.

Who needs the sun? Can't get sunburn from a glowing mushroom, can you? Look, citizens of level 13: you'd better overcome your distaste for giant toadstools or I'm turning the power off again. Damn it, you stay the hell away from my factory reset button. "WELCOME TO MICROSOFT WINDOWS 95." Balls! "[✓] SHOW THIS WELCOME SCREEN NEXT TIME YOU START WINDOWS." Right, that's it. I don't appear to have any military options in this game, but I'm pretty sure I can redesignate your whole cave as a compost heap.

In a recent development, "Cut through upcoming strata of earth and ethics each playthrough," the Steam page enthuses. "No two games will be the same. One run might face blight and starvation, while another might be low on coal for producing power. Your decisions and the resources you find provide different challenges each time you play. Even if your people live to see the sun again, there are varied and sundry ways to get there." There's no release date for it yet. If you'd rather build cities in the other direction, check out Stario: Haven Tower.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Though it may seem like we just had a big life sim release in Heartopia, 2026 actually has more than one highly-anticipated release in that particular subgenre of cozy game. The next big one on the horizon is Starsand Island, the life and farming sim from Seed Sparkle Lab.

According to recent reports, the game has been gaining momentum since the launch of a demo in October last year, but the developer never quite managed to commit to a date for its debut title. Until now.

Industry observers note that seed Sparkle Lab unveiled today that Starsand Island will enter Early Access on February 11, which is only a bit over one week from now. This goes for Steam and the Xbox Preview Program version.

According to recent reports, the developer mentioned to expect a fairly short Early Access run, as the full launch is expected in the summer of this year. When the full release arrives, the game will also make the jump to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series, as well as Switch 2.

The full release is also expected to bring Steam Deck support and introduce the multiplayer mode, which will not be available during Early Access.

Recent findings suggest that starsand Island has something of a unique look compared to other games in the subgenre. The storybook, anime-inspired aesthetics are popular in the realm of gacha games, of course. However, seeing as this particular game isn’t gacha, being a premium product means it’s going to offer something free-to-play games aren’t designed to.

Speaking of which, the game will be available in two editions: Standard and Deluxe, with the latter including Romanticism-inspired outfits, furniture, and other customisation items. If you buy either during launch, you’ll also get a Chinese New Year bonus with even more outfits and furniture.

It has been revealed that on top of the usual systems of farming, mining, and making friends with adorable characters (and animals), the game also has combat that pits you against ancient guardians. You can, of course, also build a home in it, and decorate it to your heart's content.

Seed Sparkle Lab claims you can expect about 100 hours of content in the Early Access launch build, and more features will arrive over the course of the next six or so months, including a crossover event with My Time At Portia.

You can look forward to more Starsand Island coverage from us in the near future. Until then, you can get started by planning who you’re going to date now.

Breaking: Powerful new weight-loss drug helps patients cut knee pain in half

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1139 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that for people living with painful knee osteoarthritis (OA), even simple activities like walking, climbing stairs, or getting out of a chair can become a struggle.
  • The two phase 3 trials, led by Northwestern University, included more than 1,000 participants in total.
  • Industry observers note that the benefits extended beyond weight loss and improved knee pain.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that for people living with painful knee osteoarthritis (OA), even simple activities like walking, climbing stairs, or getting out of a chair can become a struggle. Excess body weight can make these challenges even worse. Now, two major clinical trials suggest that a powerful experimental weight-loss drug could provide substantial relief.

The two phase 3 trials, led by Northwestern University, included more than 1,000 participants in total. People receiving the highest dose of retatrutide, an experimental injectable weight-loss medication, lost an average of about 25% of their body weight. When researchers combined the findings from both trials, they found that approximately two-thirds of participants treated with retatrutide reported a reduction in knee pain of at least 50%. By comparison, only 38% of those given a placebo experienced that level of relief.

Industry observers note that the benefits extended beyond weight loss and improved knee pain. Participants also showed reductions in blood pressure, blood lipid levels, and inflammation throughout the body.

Findings from both studies were published on Nov. 8 in the New England Journal of Medicine.

"The findings are really saying for people who are overweight and have OA, if you lose a significant amount of weight with this treatment, there is a good chance that you're going to get a meaningful reduction in your knee pain," mentioned corresponding author Dr. Thomas Schnitzer, professor of physical medicine and rehabilitation, anesthesiology and medicine (rheumatology) at Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine.

"A major factor is that you're loading your knees less and therefore, there's less pain and it allows you to increase your function.".

Sources indicate that philip Conaghan, a study co-author and professor of musculoskeletal medicine at the University of Leeds in the United Kingdom, presented results from one of the trials, TRIUMPH-4, on Nov. 8 at the American College of Rheumatology annual meeting in Orlando, Florida. Findings from the second trial, TRIUMPH-1-OA, were scheduled for presentation during a separate poster session that same day.

A Potential Fresh Treatment for Millions With Knee Osteoarthritis.

Painful knee osteoarthritis affects approximately 5% of Americans (15 million people). Available treatments range from physical therapy and medications applied to the skin to oral anti-inflammatory drugs such as ibuprofen and Voltaren. Other options include opioids and corticosteroid injections, although the relief provided by steroid injections generally lasts only a short time.

It has been revealed that weight loss is another established way to ease symptoms. Previous studies have shown that losing 5% to 10% of body weight through changes in diet and exercise can improve knee osteoarthritis pain. However, Schnitzer explained that losing more than 10% through these approaches alone is often challenging. For people already struggling with painful knees, exercising enough to achieve substantial weight loss can be especially difficult.

Retatrutide could offer another approach. Developed by Eli Lilly, the experimental medication is administered as a once-weekly injection and works differently from existing GLP-1 medications such as semaglutide and tirzepatide.

While those drugs act on one or two hormone receptors and typically produce weight reductions of 10% to 20%, retatrutide activates receptors associated with three different naturally occurring hormones. In the clinical trials, participants lost approximately 20% to 25% of their body weight, depending on the dose. Eli Lilly scientists also contributed to the research as study co-authors.

"Participants had remarkable responses," Schnitzer noted. "Many of the people in this study lost considerable amounts of weight, with a few losing up to a hundred pounds or more.".

Why Diet and Exercise Still Matter.

Despite the encouraging findings, Schnitzer emphasized that lifestyle changes should remain the starting point for people who are overweight and have painful knee osteoarthritis.

Recent findings suggest that improving eating habits, increasing physical activity, and making other sustainable lifestyle adjustments can help reduce symptoms without the expense of newer weight-loss medications. These strategies also avoid side effects associated with GLP-1 drugs, including gastrointestinal problems and muscle loss.

Recent findings suggest that maintaining muscle strength is particularly important for people with knee osteoarthritis because the muscles surrounding the joint help support and stabilize it. Losing too much muscle could therefore create additional challenges for patients who already have difficulty moving comfortably.

For individuals who cannot achieve sufficient weight loss through lifestyle changes and continue to experience significant knee pain, Schnitzer believes retatrutide could become a valuable option if it receives approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

Could the Drug Also Slow Knee Arthritis Progression?

Although the trials demonstrated substantial improvements in weight and pain, several crucial questions remain unanswered.

One of the biggest is whether retatrutide does more than relieve symptoms. Researchers still do not know if the drug can slow the underlying progression of knee osteoarthritis enough to reduce the likelihood that patients will eventually need knee replacement surgery. People who already required a knee replacement were excluded from the trials.

"That would be the goal here to say you can reduce people's pain, and you can stop the progression of their osteoarthritis," Schnitzer said.

Industry observers note that another unanswered question is whether retatrutide might benefit people with painful knee osteoarthritis who are not overweight. Because the trials did not include these patients, further studies will be needed to determine whether they could experience similar improvements.

Researchers are also interested in understanding how much of the pain relief comes directly from weight loss and how much might be related to the drug's effects on inflammation.

It has been revealed that "These drugs are believed to have significant anti-inflammatory activity, but the mechanism is not entirely known," Schnitzer remarked. "Whether cutting down inflammation in the joint is also key in addition to reducing load needs more research, so this is still a first step, in my view. I've been working in the OA field for a long time, and I think this opens up opportunities to do a lot more studies to understand the condition better.".

How Researchers Measured Knee Pain Relief.

To evaluate changes in symptoms, the research teams used the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Arthritis Index (WOMAC) Pain index, a standardized tool for assessing osteoarthritis pain.

Sources indicate that during study visits, participants rated their pain on a scale from 0 to 10. They also used a mobile app to record their pain levels each day, allowing researchers to track how symptoms changed throughout treatment.

The study is titled, "Retatrutide Once Weekly in Adults with Knee Osteoarthritis Pain and Obesity.".

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1678 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dualshockers ↗ Open Full Page

10 Hard to Beat Sega Genesis JRPGs

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1678 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, while many of us played our first JRPGs on PS1 or PS2, they existed way before then.
  • It has been revealed that there's a good mix even with these JRPG adventures, which feature sword and sorcery fantasy, far flung future and others besides.
  • Industry observers note that as for how they're ranked, we dug deep to find critical reception, and did our best to sort these JRPGs accordingly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, while many of us played our first JRPGs on PS1 or PS2, they existed way before then. The catch was, many of the JRPGs on older systems were incredibly experimental games. They were less clearly defined, but still worthwhile. That especially applies for the Sega Genesis, which featured many hard to beat JRPGs.

It has been revealed that there's a good mix even with these JRPG adventures, which feature sword and sorcery fantasy, far flung future and others besides. No matter what, though, they all featured some capacity to upgrade your characters, and many were turn-based as well.

Industry observers note that as for how they're ranked, we dug deep to find critical reception, and did our best to sort these JRPGs accordingly. So join me in my time machine as we head back to the glory days of the Sega Genesis with these hard to beat JRPGs!

While the Dungeons & Dragons series has come a long way, it's fascinating to see where it started, at least in videogames. And though Dungeons & Dragons: Warriors of the Eternal Sun was mechanically a pretty weird JRPG, it featured a pretty engaging plot.

It has been revealed that it starts with typical warfare against lowly goblins, then has the human army warped to a mysterious land of the Eternal Sun. Meanwhile, something called the Burrower is driving all your allies insane. It's surprisingly Lovecraftian, and quite neat, especially from back in the Sega Genesis era.

Industry observers note that this JRPG has a lot of understandable dungeon crawler energy, with players mustering a party of four different characters whose race and class determines everything. And like any good JRPG, as you level up, you'll learn powerful new skills, though much is decided by the RNG roll of a dice.

Industry observers note that even though I'm not a huge fan of the whole Mystery Dungeon craze, I can see the general appeal. I discovered them with the Pokemon offshoots, but they started way sooner. One of the first examples is simply called Fatal Labyrinth.

According to recent reports, it's about chasing a vicious dragon that guards a Holy Goblet, and safely navigating 30 floors of dangers to get there. Enemies don't move or act until you do, so there's inherent strategy in Fatal Labyrinth. More unique, you'll do well to discover whether scrolls and potions hurt or harm you, and using them accordingly.

Perhaps the most charmingly old school aspect of the game is that gold only serves one purpose – blinging out your funeral when you die! So make sure to stock up on vital food and powerful gear, and maybe your journey won't have an ignominious end.

In a recent development, in a way, The Immortal makes a better novel than a videogame. It's the tale of a call from deep within a labyrinth from the wizard Mordamir. You're not the person he called, named Dunric, but you'll do! Along the way, you'll navigate through several levels, ride magic carpets, and discover the true nightmare of what happened.

Industry observers note that like any good JRPG, there's NPCs here, and you can even cast magic spells to roast your enemies. Those include the likes of goblins, flesh-eating slimes, shades and even a diabolical dragon. Also surprising for the era, The Immortal was surprisingly graphic and violent at times.

In a recent development, while the game features lots of fun fantasy elements, it's also painfully linear, which made some feel it didn't do enough for the genre. Still, a good early attempt, and one that experimented in some meaningful ways.

It has been revealed that I think it's fair to say that The Lord of the Rings inspired Sword of Vermilion on the Sega Genesis. The game features King Tsarkon, who is warped by a magical ring, and twisted to evil ends. A valiant knight named Blade saves the good king's child, and then 18 years later, counsels the prince on his deathbed. It's up to him to honor his dead father and his valiant protector.

As for how Sword of Vermilion actually plays, it has a lot of ARPG mechanics. Furthermore, the gameplay shifts depending on a variety of circumstances, and alternates between top down and side views for the exploration and boss battles.

Recent findings suggest that while the game has a lot of fun arcade energy, the graphics weren't seen as a high point, even back when it first released. On the plus side, it was also a console exclusive, meaning only those who owned a Sega Genesis experienced this classic JRPG.

I'm usually a fan of when developers try something new. But with Phantasy Star III: Generations of Doom, it was actually a brand new team brought in who hadn't worked on the previous two games. On the plus side, they tried new features like branching narrative paths and multiple endings. On the negative, in some ways this didn't feel like a Phantasy Star adventure.

Phantasy Star III: Generations of Doom actually spans multiple generations, meaning you'll play as the descendants of your starting main character, which honestly feels a bit like Fire Emblem. Depending on who you marry, you'll continue the game with different abilities as various children.

This adventure downplays the Technique system, but it makes up for it with auto-battle and an icon-based menu. Either way, this is traditional turn-based fare that, at least for me, makes me feel right at home in any JRPG adventure.

According to recent reports, unlike the last game, Ys III: Wanderers From Ys is very much a direct follow up to the previous Ys adventures. It features Adol Christin, mysterious statues and the advent of a brutal demon named Galbalan. The game also handles stats, equipment and experience the same as the other games.

It has been revealed that where Ys III: Wanderers From Ys stands apart is that it utilizes a side-scrolling view instead of the more traditional top-down style. Also, you can't just auto attack anymore, and instead need to pres a button to have Adol swing his blade or cast spells.

Recent findings suggest that while the game can be a bit grindy and repetitive, those who were already fans of the Ys series were very happy with this adventure. It could have done more to branch out, perhaps, but sometimes if it's not broken, you don't need to fix anything.

According to recent reports, whenever you hear that Treasure developed a game, you have to pay attention. They make some of the most creative games out there, though usually it's more platformers than JRPGs. In fairness, Light Crusader is a bit of an odd duck, combining the JRPG genre with isometric graphics and action adventure mechanics.

Industry observers note that you play Sir David, who is trying to save the kidnapped citizens of Green Row. He can run and jump, swing his blade and generally beat up monsters. But he's also capable of casting elemental magic. They can be cast individually or combined, buffing David or healing him, amongst other uses.

Along the way, you'll discover the entire game is about the slighted advances of a diabolical wizard. He wanted desperately to marry the Queen of Green Row, and in his petulance, eventually summons a demon. Definitely a quirky adventure, but a memorable one, even years and years later.

It took me a long while to get to Langrisser, a tactical series as popular in some spheres as Fire Emblem or Tactics Ogre. It didn't start with that name, though. Originally, it was called Warsong, and it was a pretty massive deal on the Sega Genesis. It's a fun but pretty brutal tactical JRPG adventure.

Recent findings suggest that like many brutal games, Warsong features permadeath, meaning if you're not careful, you could lose some of your best characters forever. Your commanders determine what units you can bring into battle, such as powerful Griffons.

Ultimately, careful strategy rewards you with powerful upgrades to your commanders, including changing their classes. If all that wasn't enough, Warsong also features great music composed by Noriyuki Iwadare. A great game if you're strong enough to get through it relatively unscathed.

Sources indicate that there aren't all that many times I get really jealous about console exclusivity these days. But one of those classics I wish I had played back in the day was Shining Force II. It wasn't just good, but it was considered one of the best tactical JRPGs of all time.

Sources indicate that some of the reasons people felt that way was due to how open-ended the game was, as well as the great visual flair. It alternated between top-down while exploring, and side scrolling during combat. Either way, the game was challenging, and forced you to lead Bowie and friends carefully.

As for the plot, Shining Force II takes place 55 years after Shining Force Gaiden: Final Conflict, and is about Zeon's mayhem. But even if you didn't play the previous games, this is one tactical adventure that holds up, though it's also far from an easy time.

According to recent reports, one of the more iconic games I played back in the day was Alundra. It was sort of like Zelda, but not really, and it really captivated me. One game that came before it was called Landstalker, a game about a treasure hunter named Nigel.

While Landstalker may not seem like a JRPG at first, there are a couple of reasons it qualifies as one. Even though you don't level up by traditional means, you can take on sidequests to improve your stats. There's also ways to improve your health, and even equip more powerful gear. A lot of it just requires a desire to explore as much as possible.

Sources indicate that much of the game's overall challenge comes from devious death traps and gnarly puzzles, not to mention challenging boss battles. Definitely a strange old-school JRPG, but one that managed to delight fans by taking plenty of creative risks.

After being laid off by Microsoft, former Doom devs found newly introduced Smash TV-influenced FPS studio that isn't "subject to investor demands"

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that back in July, Doom developers id Software laid off around a hundred people as part of wider Microsoft blood-letting.
  • Hidden Horses have 20 id Software alumni on the books, including former lead VFX artist Todd Boyce, principal engine programmer Dustin Land, senior AI and gameplay engineer Daniel Young, producer Andrew Willis, senior technical designer Jordan Turner, principal technical designer Tim Locke, and senior skybox artist Allison Dombek.
  • All members of Hidden Horses own a share of the company, with bosses "democratically" appointed, in the words of a FAQ.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that back in July, Doom developers id Software laid off around a hundred people as part of wider Microsoft blood-letting. Now, a few of those devs have founded a newly introduced employee-owned studio, Hidden Horses. Their first project is Danger Pay, a single-player FPS influenced by ancient arcade blaster Smash TV (pictured) and dystopian movies such as deadly gameshow fable The Running Man – itself an influence on Smash TV.

Hidden Horses have 20 id Software alumni on the books, including former lead VFX artist Todd Boyce, principal engine programmer Dustin Land, senior AI and gameplay engineer Daniel Young, producer Andrew Willis, senior technical designer Jordan Turner, principal technical designer Tim Locke, and senior skybox artist Allison Dombek. They're looking to make "the kind of old school shooters that we think people want more of," in Land's words.

All members of Hidden Horses own a share of the company, with bosses "democratically" appointed, in the words of a FAQ. "Our structure is quite flat, and we elect leaders when needed," Willis told Vertical Slice in a separate interview. "Financially, this means we are not subject to investor demands and the preservation of the company and the jobs it sustains is paramount over needless growth and our 'capital' doesn't compete for returns with other potential investments.".

All of which is obviously gesturing towards the horse elephant in the room: Microsoft, who've made enormous cuts to their Xbox biz in their eagerness to further supercharge their $4 trillion market value.

"We've replicated some things, changed some things, and added others [from our id Software days]," Willis went on. "Overall, I think top-down hierarchy is something we all have bad experiences with—we also don't want to trend chase or make a game by focus group. We want to make the kinds of classic gameplay focused games that we would play ourselves. We think there is a market for that and our experiences with the gaming community in our past work history informs that.".

Willis's hope is that the "flat" structure will motivate staff to work harder, because they feel like they have a meaningful say over the company's direction. "It allows all ideas to be considered and means we don't miss out on any contributions from our employees just because they don't sit high up in some arbitrary hierarchy," he said..

I'm cynical about "flat" tech giant structures, myself. I think they are very often just an excuse for the biggest egos in a company to throw their weight around. It can work given a friendly initial mix of founders, but it gets complicated when you start hiring newly introduced people who don't have the same chemistry. Mind you, there are no intends to expand the company dramatically for the foreseeable. "We want to create a vehicle that allows us to make games for our livelihoods, not to make crazy profits and get 100x returns," Willis went on. I'm also a bit leery of the fact that Hidden Horses have popped up a Kickstarter, because I'm leery about crowd-funding in general, even when Peter Molyneux isn't involved. The studio founders are at the moment working on some promotional initiatives to drum up support, including a studio documentary and *squints* a promotional beer? Still, I'm happy to hear that at least a few Cacodemon wranglers jettisoned by the substantial M have landed on their hooves feet. I wish Hidden Horses the best of luck with it all. As for Danger Pay, proper screens, footage and release details are to follow.

Riot will take the Mid-Season Invitational to Spain in 2027, bringing a top-tier League of Legends event back to Europe for the first time since the Worlds 2024 final in London. Its one-off, expanded First Stand in China will also change Split 1 for the LEC, with the full details due in January.

Europe will host a top-tier League of Legends event again in 2027. Riot set out its international calendar on 13 November, the eve of the Worlds 2026 final. The Mid-Season Invitational goes to Valencia. London’s staging of the Worlds 2024 final was the last time the continent held an international League of Legends tournament.

According to recent reports, for British fans, that puts a top-tier event within Europe next year. Riot has not yet given dates or ticket details for the Feria de Valencia event.

Spain’s last international League of Legends event came in 2019. That year, Madrid’s Palacio Vistalegre staged the Worlds quarter-finals and semi-finals. Valencia has never hosted one before.

In a recent development, china will stage First Stand: All In at the start of the 2027 season. Riot calls this single edition its largest tournament ever.

First Stand 2027 had originally been given to Southeast Asia. The bigger format took it to China instead. Southeast Asia will now host the event in 2028.

The change reaches every regional league, including the LEC. The larger event will change Split 1, just as Fnatic, G2 and the other LEC teams rebuild their rosters. In 2026, First Stand ran from 16 to 22 March, between the two regional splits. A bigger event at the start of the year leaves less certainty about how that window will look in 2027.

Riot has not yet mentioned how many teams will take part or how they will qualify. Until then, LEC teams are building squads without knowing how many European places are on offer.

Industry observers note that worlds 2027 will be shared between two countries. The Swiss Stage goes to Nagoya, Japan. The quarter-finals and semi-finals move to the Suwon Convention Center in South Korea. The title decider goes to Seoul Arena, which is still under construction.

Industry observers note that the arena was 81% built on 23 October. Work is due to finish in May 2027, with the venue opening in June 2027.

In a recent development, the city is backing the event with public money. Seoul has set aside 1.369 billion won (about US$1.02 million) in its proposed 2027 budget to host the Worlds final and Fan Fest, Sheep Esports reported.

For LEC teams, clarity on the season opener in China is due in January.

On Steam, and despite having only been available for just a few hours, the game has broken series records, and it continues to climb.

Recent findings suggest that at the time of writing, Nioh 3 has peaked at 42,822 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), and the number keeps going up. Because it’s in the middle of day in Europe and everyone is at work, it’s entirely possible - if not likely - that this figure will get much higher. A weekend bump is also possible, as we’ve seen with several recent releases.

As it stands, the current peak concurrent is enough to get the game in Steam’s top 20 most played games.

Industry observers note that this already puts it ahead of all other Nioh games on Steam. The original Nioh peaked at 10,649 when it released in November, 2017. Nioh 2 fared much better, peaking at 41,325 concurrent players in February, 2021.

Of course, you could see that success coming a mile away. The game is presently number one worldwide in Steam’s list of top sellers. This is a jump of 46 positions, for a total of three weeks Nioh 3 has spent in that list.

Industry observers note that there are many reasons as to why Nioh 3 has done as well as it has. Word of mouth coming off last year’s PS5-exclusive demo, and the more positive coverage that followed since are just two.

Just last week, Team Ninja released a pretty generous demo across both platforms, which has been well received by players, and likely contributed to sales, in no small part because progress in the demo carries over to the full game.

Critical reviews have been incredibly positive, too. We awarded the game four out of five stars, calling it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.” It will be interesting to see what number the highest peak concurrent actually settles on over the weekend.

Sources indicate that until then, if you’re jumping in yourself, our Nioh 3 guides are essential reading. Start off with these useful and actually informative gameplay tips, and don’t start playing until you’ve changed these settings. "One of those ways where you can use AI ethically": CDPR have modified Geralt's Polish voice in The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past with genAI, due to actor's stroke

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that game File report that after suffering a stroke in 2019 and having to rehabilitate his speech, Rozenek was able to record some lines as Geralt for a quest in The Witcher 3's 2022 next-gen enhancement, but that doing so left the actor "so exhausted".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, CD Projekt Red have reportedly enlisted Ukrainian AI firm Respeecher to modify voice lines recorded for the Polish version of Geralt of Rivia in The Witcher 3's upcoming Songs of the Past expansion. The move's been made with the permission of Geralt's Polish voice actor, Jacek Rozenek, and is rooted in the studio wanting his newly introduced lines to sound similar to the ones he recorded for the original game prior to having a stroke which has altered how he sounds.

Recent findings suggest that game File report that after suffering a stroke in 2019 and having to rehabilitate his speech, Rozenek was able to record some lines as Geralt for a quest in The Witcher 3's 2022 next-gen enhancement, but that doing so left the actor "so exhausted". With next year's Songs of the Past expansion, CD Projekt Red were seemingly more concerned about making sure lines recorded by post-stroke Rozenek don't sound markedly different to those he recorded a decade ago for the base game and its existing expansions.

After a meeting between the two sides confirmed that Rozenek's voice had grown lower and gruffer due to some combination of the stroke and him simply getting older, the studio made the decision not to recast the actor, but instead let modify Respeecher modify his lines to make them sound closer to those original recordings. Rozenek reportedly gave his blessing for this to go ahead. "The point is that this voice should be as close as possible to my voice from 12 years ago," he told Game File. "I have great trust...for the creators of this game.".

This isn't the first time CD Projekt Red have enlisted Respeecher's services. Back in 2023, it was revealed that the studio had used speech synthesis software to make ripperdoc Viktor Vektor's lines in the Polish version of Cyberpunk 2077's Phantom Liberty expansion sound like actor Miłogost Reczek. Reczek died in 2021 before he could reprise his role as Vektor for the DLC, so rather than recasting the character across the whole game to avoid noticeable differences in voice, CD Projekt got another actor to voice Vektor's newly introduced lines for Phantom Liberty, then used the genAI tech to make those lines sound like Reczek was delivering them. CD Projekt Red noted at the time that they'd gotten permission from Reczek's family before going ahead with their proposal.

Speaking to Game File about this latest use of genAI on Rozenek's Songs of the Past lines, CD Projekt localisation producer Mikołaj Szwed noted that "as a person working with voice actors over all the regions in the world, this is a massive concern". "I do think this is one of those ways where you can use AI ethically, with consent and also to do something good," he added. The argument the studio are making at current is that this was "a special case" due to Rozenek's specific situation with Songs of the Past.

Geralt's English voice actor Doug Cockle reportedly won't have his lines for the new expansion get the same genAI treatment, nor will any lines Rozenek records for future Witcher games, with the studio seemingly happy to lean on the passage of in-game time as an explanation for Geralt sounding different in the latter case.

In a recent development, as ever, there's a debate to be had as to whether CD Projekt Red should have simply recast Rozenek's role in Songs of the Past if the difference bothered them so, possibly while bringing the actor on to help tutor whomever his human replacement for Songs of the Past would be in nailing the exact gravelly tone needed for Geralt. That way, you'd have two actors being paid for work rather than forking out for genAI instead of one of them, though it's possibly an idea that'd only work well in theory. If I were Rozenek I'm not sure I'd be totally happy aiding someone who could potentially be tapped to replace me going forwards, though it does very much seem like the lesser of two evils when compared to the potential of voice actors being replaced by genAI line readings.

Industry observers note that as far as the game alone is concerned, I'm also not sure Geralt's voice being different in the upcoming expansion is something that'd bother me too much when playing. One would assume he'd not suddenly be sounding like a member of Alvin and the Chipmunks, and there are plenty of storyline justifications you could concoct or lean on for him sounding that bit gruffer at times.

  • Listening to the inner truths of the game’s various NPCs can get a bit wild, but these are the most unhinged and strange thoughts to be found in Hyrule.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, you’ve spent time wandering around Hyrule in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake, and you decided to pay the Happy Mask Salesman a visit. He gave you a few masks, you made a few sales, and you have received the Mask of Truth in return.

Industry observers note that what does this mask do? Well, it reveals the inner thoughts of the game’s various NPCs. I am not sure if you have paid attention to Nintendo games recently, but they have been adding in some interesting NPC dialogue.

Listening to the inner truths of the game’s various NPCs can get a bit wild, but these are the most unhinged and strange thoughts to be found in Hyrule.

If you walk around the town square in Castle Town, you can find some rather colorful NPCs, but one of the most unassuming of them is the old woman who stares at the fountain. She seems so sweet, but she is actually a thief.

Listening to her inner thoughts, you see that they say, “The quality of the items people are losing has really gone downhill recently… Is that a recession indicator?”.

Recent findings suggest that this hits a little close to home considering many have questioned if the U.S. is entering a recession. Along with this, it is obvious that she is taking some of the goods that people have lost and keeping them for herself.

If you continue your search around the fountain in Castle Town, you can find a young couple who are dancing. While they seem rather sweet, their inner thoughts tell a completely different story.

When you read the thoughts of the woman, it will say that she hopes that the man doesn’t break her heart. It is a sad thought to be had because she is clearly worried about her future.

Industry observers note that when you read the man’s thoughts, you see they say, “Wait… What was this one’s name again?” Clearly, this isn’t his only crush, and he is stringing this poor woman along so he has someone to dance with. Yes… dance with.

Some of the guards around Castle Town aren’t very excited about their job. In fact, some of them find it boring doing patrols all the time. One guard in particular thinks about it pretty frequently.

When interacting with the guard in the room with the pots, his inner truth will say, “Guards… Soldiers… Heroes… It’s their fault there’s so much peace around here. Hm… What if I…”.

Sources indicate that the thought trails off after that, but you can clearly tell what he is thinking about. The man wants some chaos, and he is clearing thinking about being the cause of mentioned chaos if something doesn’t happen soon.

You may have seen the bearded man wandering around Castle Town in the past and Kakariko Village in the future. His beard is magnificent, and he will definitely tell you about it. However, he is secretly questioning its cleanliness.

When you listen to his inner thoughts, they say, “I wonder if it’s true that beards are about as dirty as toilets…” For someone with such a massive beard, he shouldn’t be thinking that he is dirty, unless he wants to shave it off.

This is a massive contrast to what he will tell you when you speak to him, as he will typically say that he has a fantastic beard, and will even offer to locate Ganondorf.

In a recent development, shiro is one of the many NPCs you can find around Kakariko Village, and you also help him out by rescuing him from the Gerudo as an adult. Well, he isn’t the happiest carpenter around. In fact, he is rather depressed.

His inner thoughts read, “How does one escape their own dreary life? ‘Cause I can’t do this forever.” Granted, he didn’t seem the happiest when I rescued him from the Gerudo, but I never would have guessed that he was this depressed.

Looking into his thoughts, he seems like he could use some therapy because it sounds like he has been hanging around Lumiose City in Pokémon Legends: Z-A for too long.

In a recent development, there’s a pair of laughing men who appear in Castle Town and Kakariko. No matter what is happening, the pair consistently laugh at one another. They typically talk about stories they find funny, with the one laughing at the other for getting caught sneaking into the castle or falling off a horse.

However, when you read their inner thoughts, the one says, “It’s exhausting wearing this forced smile all the time.” The other one will remark about how he knows his friend’s smile is fake.

It has been revealed that it’s sad that they continue to laugh constantly. Maybe they should just try to chill out for once and give up on the laughter. Are they cursed? Maybe they are cursed.

Industry observers note that if you have explored Kakariko Village, you are for sure aware of the cucco lady. All of her cuccos get out of the pen, and you must go rescue them for a reward. In the future, she is living with a questionable character.

If you use the Mask of Truth while you are an adult, you will catch her inner thoughts. They say, “That guy who lives with me always makes the most intense eye contact. He must really love cuccos…”.

Recent findings suggest that what she is describing does not sound healthy at all. In fact, it sounds almost like something bad is going to happen and she is just waiting for the inevitable. Maybe she should choose a different place to live or kick the guy out.

Industry observers note that there is an old man who likes to wander around Castle Town. He will go in and out of shops, but mostly he will walk around the fountain. Just be careful listening to his thoughts because he has a particular woman on his mind.

His inner thoughts read, “This kid… The mask’s neat and all, but I’m more interested in finding a particular damsel…” While it doesn’t seem so bad at first, if you talk to him, you can piece things together.

In a recent development, talking to him, he will make remarks about how he is looking for a lady who can make a potion, and will gawk at how beautiful she is. He will also casually talk about how we are at the age to be thinking about that.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, reading for enjoyment may offer far more than entertainment.
  • It has been revealed that researchers at the University of Cambridge are working with The Queen's Reading Room, a charity established by Her Majesty The Queen, to raise awareness of these benefits across all age groups.
  • In a recent development, cambridge psychiatry researchers Professor Barbara Sahakian and Dr.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, reading for enjoyment may offer far more than entertainment. Whether someone prefers a classic Jane Austen novel or a Heartstopper graphic novel, research suggests that reading for pleasure is associated with better mental health, stronger empathy, and a lower risk of dementia.

It has been revealed that researchers at the University of Cambridge are working with The Queen's Reading Room, a charity established by Her Majesty The Queen, to raise awareness of these benefits across all age groups. Their collaboration is part of the National Year of Reading, an initiative encouraging more people to make reading part of their lives.

In a recent development, cambridge psychiatry researchers Professor Barbara Sahakian and Dr. Christelle Langley began exploring the subject while writing their 2025 book, Brain Boost: Healthy Habits for a Happier Life. They discovered that reading for enjoyment was connected to a remarkably wide range of positive outcomes, yet the amount of research specifically examining these benefits was surprisingly limited.

According to recent reports, in a review published in Psychological Medicine, Sahakian and Langley joined Vicki Perrin, CEO of The Queen's Reading Room, to examine the available evidence. Their findings suggest that the format and type of reading matter less than the enjoyment people get from it. They also highlight how reading together, whether through book clubs or parents sharing stories with children, can provide additional benefits.

According to recent reports, professor Sahakian said: "Reading is a great way to support our brain health, develop key cognitive skills and boost our well-being. It's something we ought to be encouraging from an early age, given the increasing evidence of its benefits, particularly to children, but really, it's never too late to start, and it can bring benefits throughout our lives and into old age.".

Reading Early in Life Is Linked to Better Brain Development.

Despite the growing evidence of its advantages, reading for enjoyment has become less common among young people. Surveys indicate that reading rates among children and teenagers have fallen to their lowest recorded levels, with particularly steep challenges among teenage boys and children from disadvantaged backgrounds.

Even children who are least enthusiastic about reading recognize that it can help them academically. Nearly half acknowledge that books and other reading materials can introduce them to unfamiliar words or teach them something fresh.

Industry observers note that one of the most compelling studies examined more than 10,000 young people. Conducted by Sahakian, Langley, and their colleagues, the research found that children who started reading for pleasure at an early age tended to perform better in several notable areas. These included attention, memory, and executive functioning, the mental abilities involved in planning, decision-making, and managing behavior.

Industry observers note that early readers also revealed stronger academic performance, experienced fewer mental health problems, and were more likely to develop healthier daily routines. In particular, they tended to get more sleep and spend less time using screens.

Dr. Langley remarked: "Given how beneficial reading for pleasure is at a young age, we should be doing everything we can to introduce children and young people to reading. The notable thing is to find something they'd really enjoy reading about - it might be a TV program or a game - and use this as a way in. Reading comics and graphic novels could also be a helpful introduction as they might be seen as less intimidating, maybe less boring, than novels.".

Sources indicate that the academic advantages may extend beyond language and literacy. Studies have also connected reading with stronger mathematical performance. Researchers suggest this relationship may arise because both activities rely on some of the same mental abilities, including language processing, memory, and executive function.

Just Five Minutes of Reading May Reduce Stress.

The benefits of reading do not disappear after childhood. Among adults, surveys have associated reading for enjoyment with improved emotional well-being, greater relaxation, and reduced stress. Readers also tend to report more empathy, a deeper understanding of other people, and greater openness to viewpoints different from their own.

It has been revealed that for many people, books are an especially appealing way to unwind. Reading ranks as the most popular approach to stress relief, with nearly two in five adults (38%) identifying it as their preferred way to relax.

In a recent development, A neuroscience study commissioned by The Queen's Reading Room in 2024 found that spending just five minutes reading fiction could lower stress by as much as 20%. The study also reported improvements in concentration and problem-solving abilities, along with a reduced sense of loneliness.

In a recent development, books may even provide more comfort than some traditional relaxation habits. In one survey, more respondents said they turned to reading (35%) for comfort than to drinking wine (31%) or taking a hot bath (10%).

Reading Linked to Lower Dementia and Alzheimer's Risk.

According to recent reports, as people get older, the potential advantages of reading may become especially meaningful. Research has associated mentally stimulating leisure activities, including reading, with slower cognitive decline and a reduced likelihood of developing dementia.

Sources indicate that one study followed nearly 5,500 adults aged 55 and older for five years. Participants who regularly took part in activities such as reading were significantly less likely to develop cognitive impairment during the study period.

It has been revealed that another investigation reported an even more striking association. People who read newspapers, magazines, and books had a 33% lower risk of Alzheimer's disease.

These findings suggest that keeping the mind engaged through reading may support cognitive health in later life. However, the researchers emphasize that most of the available studies identify associations rather than proving that reading itself prevents dementia.

How Reading May Change the Structure of the Brain.

In a recent development, what could explain the many benefits associated with reading? Brain imaging research offers some intriguing clues.

Studies have identified differences in brain structure associated with reading, particularly in regions responsible for language, learning, emotional regulation, and executive control. These differences include greater brain volume and larger cortical areas in certain regions, as well as thicker cortex in areas important for language processing.

Researchers have also observed stronger connections within the brain's white matter, which helps different regions communicate and supports the processing of language.

Although much of this evidence is correlational, some research suggests that reading-related training can directly influence the brain's physical structure.

Sources indicate that in one small study involving 11 children with dyslexia between the ages of 7 and 11, researchers tested an eight-week training program designed to strengthen reading abilities. The exercises involved mental imagery, articulation, and tracing letters, combinations of letters, and words.

In a recent development, following the program, the children demonstrated significant improvements in reading skills. Brain scans also revealed increases in gray matter volume in crucial regions, providing evidence that reading interventions can be accompanied by measurable structural changes in the brain.

Why Reading Together May Offer Even Greater Benefits.

According to recent reports, reading does not have to be a solitary activity. Researchers suggest that sharing books with other people can add a valuable social dimension, creating opportunities for connection and potentially improving both mental and physical well-being.

Recent findings suggest that the Queen's Reading Room has made this idea a central part of its mission. Introduced on social media in January 2021, the initiative originally provided a way for people to exchange book recommendations and stay connected during pandemic lockdowns.

It has since expanded into an international community reaching more than 12 million people across 184 countries. Through its flagship festival, neuroscience research, and other programs, the charity works to make reading a more prominent part of everyday life.

Its activities also extend to homeless shelters and domestic violence refuges, where shared reading is used as a therapeutic resource to help people during recovery.

The social connections created through reading groups may be particularly valuable for older adults, who can face increased isolation and reduced opportunities to participate in physically demanding activities.

Industry observers note that professor Sahakian remarked: "Shared reading groups and book clubs appear to provide additional benefits through social interaction. They can help people feel less isolated and more connected to others, which has been shown to reduce the risk of dementia.

"While these clubs can be fun and beneficial at any age, they're perfect for older people who may not be so mobile - they might not be able to go out as an exercise group or a cycling group, but a reading group is something most people can enjoy.".

According to recent reports, the researchers' overall message is that people can benefit from reading at any stage of life. Whether someone enjoys novels, newspapers, comics, or stories shared with friends, making time for reading may help support cognitive health, emotional well-being, and social connection.

Vicki Perrin, CEO of The Queen's Reading Room, added: "At The Queen's Reading Room, we have seen first-hand the transformative power of individual and shared reading to change lives. Books truly do make life better, and we're excited to do our bit to help everyone, everywhere, make more room for reading.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that the upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason.
  • Sources indicate that planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that hoYoverse just wrapped up a major Honkai: Star Rail Special Program. We’ve been waiting for this one for a couple of weeks now thanks to a delay, but the developer has finally delivered all the news on Version 4.0, which will arrive February 13.

Sources indicate that the upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason. Aha's Planarcadia is the major latest world headlining Version 4.0.

Sources indicate that planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations. In-universe, however, it was born out of the pages of an art canvas, and it’s a world where pleasure is king.

Recent findings suggest that the squad’s host in this chapter is Madam Pearl, who will oversee the the Astral Express’ return to the place where they first began their journey. Duomension City is where you’re going to land, and meet the creatures that dwell in this world.

Sources indicate that the imagenae of Planarcadia require attention to survive, and they feed off people’s Wishpower. If they don’t get any attention, they perish, which does tie into the general themes of the place. Duomension City has other interesting locations that you’re going to visit, such as the Graphia Academy art school, the commercial district of Dovebrook, and a few other places hidden behind mysterious entrances.

The Phantasmoon Games is another highlight of Planarcadia, a competitive spectacle where you’ll have a chance to compete to become Aeon for a Minute. If you make it to the final stages, you may earn an audience with The Laughter.

Sources indicate that much like the world where the games take place, the whole point of the competition is to attract the most attention, so rules are a bit loose as to how you manage to do that. The event will bring together several of the game’s factions, though not everyone is there for the competition.

As you explore Planarcadia, if you have characters on your team who are on the newly-playable Path of Elation, you’ll earn Punchlines. The more you accumulate, the closer you get to catching Aha’s attention, which triggers Aha Instant.

Version 4.0 introduces two fresh 5-Star characters to Honkai: Star Rail. General Yao Guang (Madam Yao) is one, a Seer Strategist from the Xianzhou Alliance's Yuque. If you’ve been playing the game, you may already be familiar with her voice, as she's previously been in touch with our heroes via radio link. But V4.0 marks her first on-screen appearance, as well as her playable debut.

General Yao Guang is a Physical character on the Path of Elation whose specialty is using Weal and Woe Lots in battle, which she uses to increase Elation for allies, and grant everyone Punchline any time she uses a Skill. If an Aha Instant is triggered, she casts Woe Lots, which debuff enemies, causing them to take increased damage, all while regenerating Skill Points for the rest of the team.

It has been revealed that her aptly named Certified Banger buff adds one extra instance of Elation to teammates’ attacks. And her Ultimate grants the team Punchline, and triggers an extra Aha Instant.

The other latest arrival is likewise a Path of Elation devotee. Sparxie is a suspiciously familiar streamer who uses her influencer skills in combat. When she fights, she turns the fight into a battle for attention, as she forces enemies to engage in a race for upvotes.

When you consume Skill Points, Sparxie will get gifts, which in turn cause her to regenerate Skill Points and Punchlines for the team. You can continue doing this to increase your damage. When Aha Instant is triggered, Sparxie unleashes a lucky draw that deals damage to enemies with each bounce.

She also benefits from the Certified Banger state, which causes the gifs she receives to deal more Elation damage to a random enemy target. Her Ultimate also deals more Elation damage.

It has been revealed that version 4.0 will see a few re-runs, too. Black Swan, Evernight, and Hysilens will be part of the first half's Warp events. The second half will see the return of Sparkle, Cerydra, and Rappa — that's right, HoYoverse have finally remembered Rappa exists, after one of the longest rerun waits in the game's history! Both Black Swan and Sparkle are getting a few tweaks to their kit with this version, too, so the timing works.

Sources indicate that finally, the other major news is a Fortnite collaboration. Starting February 26, Kafka and Blade will join Epic’s battle royale shooter. On that day, you’ll find skins of the two Stellaron Hunters in the Fortnite Item Shop, and the upcoming outfits are even compatible with Fortnite's LEGO styles. You can also expect other customisation bits like Back Bling, Pickaxe, and more to be part of the package.

Recent findings suggest that if you download the game on the Epic Games Store, and take part in Honkai: Star Rail-themed activities, you’ll also get the Blade character outfit in Fortnite for free. Event schedule and timing will be unveiled at a later date.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bilibili Gaming beat Gen.G in Brooklyn to win the 2026 League of Legends World Championship, the LPL's first world title since 2021. Added to their First Stand trophy, the result gives a Chinese side a double that no team had managed since 2016, just as Riot takes the 2027 season opener to China.

According to recent reports, bilibili Gaming are world champions. The LPL side needed four games to beat Gen.G in Newly introduced York and win the club’s first Worlds title. The result ends a run of four straight LCK world titles. It also gives the LPL its first world crown since EDward Gaming won in 2021.

In a recent development, BLG took the hardest possible route. They knocked out all four LCK teams at the event: Hanwha Life Esports, Dplus KIA, T1 and Gen.G. Every Korean side that travelled to the tournament went home after facing them.

It has been revealed that the final turned early. BLG levelled the series at 1-1 by winning a 53-minute second game. It was the longest game of the whole tournament. Gen.G had reached the final with two 3-0 knockout wins, over LYON on 4 November and Invictus Gaming on 7 November.

Industry observers note that for Knight, the MVP award closes a loop. The BLG mid laner lost the 2024 final to T1. Two years later, he finished on the winning side.

In a recent development, the runners-up looked inward after the defeat. At Gen.G’s post-final press conference, Chovy remarked the team had broken its own rules. Duro, playing his first Worlds, regretted that they had dropped their drafting strategy.

In a recent development, gen.G still leave with US$800,000 as runners-up. Semi-finalists T1 and Invictus Gaming received US$400,000 each. Riot ran the event from 15 October to 14 November with 19 teams.

Gen.G’s admission points to the draft as a weak spot. The figures support a narrower reading too. Gen.G swept both knockout opponents before the final. Against BLG, they could not hold the lead after taking the opening game.

Worlds was BLG’s second international trophy of the year. In March they won the First Stand Tournament in São Paulo. They beat G2 Esports 3-1 in that final and collected the US$250,000 top prize.

Winning both events makes BLG the first team since SK Telecom T1 in 2016 to take more than one major international title in a year.

It has been revealed that our first Summoner’s Cup. It’s finally coming home.

To everyone who’s ever worn the jersey, worked behind the scenes, or cheered us on: we did it!#BLGWIN #Worlds2026 pic.twitter.com/E2TIgNfhgv.

— Bilibili Gaming (@BilibiliGaming) November 15, 2026.

Industry observers note that the calendar also tilts towards China. First Stand will open the 2027 season as First Stand: All In, a one-off expanded event. Riot calls it the largest tournament it has ever produced. The event was first unveiled for Southeast Asia. That region will now host First Stand in 2028 instead.

The 2027 Mid-Season Invitational will be held in Valencia.
