    • Xbox have confirmed that Wolfenstein 3 is indeed in production at Indiana Jones and the Great Circle devs MachineGames and that Doom makers id Software have started work on their next game after losing a bunch of staff to the mass layoffs across Microsoft's gaming division this year.
    • Industry observers note that "A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations," isn't part of the marketing spiel for either of those games.
    • In a recent development, the Wolfenstein and id confirmations came as Xbox had a bit of a social media party to commemorate their 25th birthday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Xbox have confirmed that Wolfenstein 3 is indeed in production at Indiana Jones and the Great Circle devs MachineGames and that Doom makers id Software have started work on their next game after losing a bunch of staff to the mass layoffs across Microsoft's gaming division this year.

    Industry observers note that "A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations," isn't part of the marketing spiel for either of those games. Instead, it's something Xbox CEO Asha Shama has bellowed amid a rant outlining how she sees the firm's future.

    In a recent development, the Wolfenstein and id confirmations came as Xbox had a bit of a social media party to commemorate their 25th birthday. Sharma, ever keen to be seen right next to any positive news coming out of the company, confirmed Wolfenstein 3 is in production by posting a photo showing a few lines from its script. Around the same time, she shouted out Doom: The Dark Ages Revelations' incoming Slaughter Mode, adding that "the team is already working on its next game".

    The official id Software account responded to note that this next game is being made by their "teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin", and that "it'll be some time before [they're] ready to share more".

    We're incredibly excited about our next project, a new game from our teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin. It'll be some time before we're ready to share more but we can't wait for you to see what we're working on.

    Sources indicate that alongside hollering about these couple of games, Sharma put out a 25th anniversary statement which for the most part does the sort of bigging up of Xbox's past you'd expect. Good times were had, we blazed a trail and made lots of money, etcetera. The final section saw the exec attempt to look forward to the next 25 years for Xbox.

    "While modern games demonstrate the heights of human craft in ways unimaginable just decades ago, the cost, resources, and risk required to create them have grown just as dramatically," she wrote. "As a result, too many ideas never become games, and too many games fall short of what their creators imagined. For decades, this has been the unavoidable tradeoff of ambition. We must change this.

    Industry observers note that "Throughout human history, the scale of what we could create was determined by the people, capital, and resources we could command. That relationship is beginning to break. A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations. A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today's games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982.".

    Recent findings suggest that that certainly sounds a lot like the sales pitch the biggest proponents of generative AI keep wheeling out, while avoiding saying generative AI out loud in the hopes of making it more palatable to folks who might not make the connection. I'm waiting for Sharma to put out another post revealing that she accidentally mixed another section of the Wolfenstein script into her celebratory musings, but I'm not holding my breath.

    Xbox parent organization Microsoft are still right now subject to a BDS movement boycott over their reported ties to the Israeli military.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Even before the game came out, it was pretty easy to guess that Nioh 3 would be a hit. From the word of mouth leading up to launch, to the well-received free demo, there was little chance the action RPG wasn’t going to be a major deal.

    Recent findings suggest that today, publisher Koei Tecmo has confirmed that the game has officially passed over one million copies sold worldwide across PC, and PlayStation 5. This makes it the fastest in the Nioh franchise to reach this milestone.

    As a result of this fantastic launch, Nioh 3 has now pushed overall Nioh franchise sales to be over 10 million, which includes the original Nioh as well as Nioh 2. Today’s news comes just two weeks after the game arrived on PC, and PS5.

    According to recent reports, on Steam, where it’s available on PC, it shot up the Steam charts, and immediately broke the series’ previous best peak concurrent player count record. From there, the numbers kept growing, leading up to a stellar weekend where it peaked at 88,045 concurrent players on Steam, double that of its launch day.

    This now stands as the largest for any Nioh game on Steam, and though we don’t have insight into how well it’s doing on PS5 specifically, it still shows that the Nioh series continues to grow.

    Recent findings suggest that nioh 3 builds on everything the two prior games established, and pushes the series into the semi-open-world realm, with several larger maps that each cover a period of time in Japan’s history. In our Nioh 3 review we called it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.”.

    If you’re curious about the challenging and very rewarding action RPG, start with these gameplay tips, and don’t be shy to call upon a friend (or stranger) for help using our co-op guide.

    • It has been revealed that in development for years, and running on a custom C++ engine, Horu is inspired by 2006 hybrid RTS Star Wars: Empire at War - good, not great, in the words of turncoat jankonaut Graham, and the subject of many mods.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that clicking a random link this morning, I was dazzled by the glare of a thousand laser batteries firing simultaneously. My ears trembled beneath the trundle of a million caterpillar tracks. Balls of ice, bolts of lightning, shipments of rare alloys, and cascades of drop pods went screaming down my nerves and detonated in my frontal cortex, painting starlanes across the inside of my skull. "Oh god, they've finally found us!" I yelled, hiding beneath my desk. "I for one welcome our new galactic overlords!".

    It has been revealed that but then I realised that I wasn't looking at a live newsfeed, but merely the Steam page for Horu, a real-time 4X strategy game in which you can "command hundreds of thousands of units across land and space", in the summary of developer David "GlassBeaver" Nadaski. There's also a magic system, this being "the spice that makes your enemy's defeat bitter", which is a very genteel way to characterise glaciating a tank formation or conjuring a miniature blackhole.

    It has been revealed that in development for years, and running on a custom C++ engine, Horu is inspired by 2006 hybrid RTS Star Wars: Empire at War - good, not great, in the words of turncoat jankonaut Graham, and the subject of many mods. Horu's way of bettering Empire at War is seemingly to add a shedload more of everything. You can engage in a fleet battle that looks like two migrating ant hives colliding, even as a frankly unnecessary quantity of cyborgs pour over the forgeworld beneath and get their shit kicked in by some tornado-summoning sorcerers.

    Offensives appear to work like this: any drop ships that push through the fleet battle add meat to the ground invasion, with the option of deploying wormholes to sneak your troops behind the defending armada. On the ground, you're basically out to capture control points. You're allegedly spared from "continuous babysitting" by semi-autonomous squadron commanders and an orders system that lets you queue up objectives, before units engage in battle.

    You can still give individual orders to units, but that seems like a recipe for acute wrist injury. There's also a boarding action mechanic whereby your hijackers move through vessels room by room. Again, I struggle to understand how you'll have time and dexterity to oversee such skulduggery when there are a bajillion particle cannons going off all at once.

    In a recent development, outside of combat, there are planets to develop, shipyards to build, spy networks to groom, research trees to water, and stock markets to manipulate. It all looks like business as usual for an imperial 4X. Honestly, I can imagine the maximalist warfaring being a hot mess, and then there's the fact that the dev is running a Kickstarter "to fund the remaining assets needed for a playable build: more spaceships, more units, more animations, more sounds, more music, and everything in between." I've been burned by Kickstarter overpromising before. Still, I can only admire the vindictive intellect that would have me play a little game of FTL inside what looks like one of the larger PvP scraps from Eve Online.

    Sources indicate that you can read more on Steam. Release date there is currently none. For an equally populous strategy experience that's closer in style to Supreme Commander, check out Sanctuary: Shattered Space.

    • The Grand Theft Auto games have always been synonymous with America; Americana is baked into the crime series' very being.

    • In an interview with The Guardian, Rockstar North co-studio boss Rob Nelson propped the proverbial door open a sliver by saying: "Never say never." He then rapidly followed that comment with: "But there’s still so much to do in America".
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Grand Theft Auto games have always been synonymous with America; Americana is baked into the crime series' very being. Across its history, there's only ever been one GTA game set outside America: the London-based expansion of the original game.

    Sources indicate that GTA 6 follows this template, parodying the American state of Florida and the city of Miami. But what about the next game - will the series always be in America? Not necessarily.

    In an interview with The Guardian, Rockstar North co-studio boss Rob Nelson propped the proverbial door open a sliver by saying: "Never say never." He then rapidly followed that comment with: "But there’s still so much to do in America".

    This is a topic Rockstar has responded to before, most notably when company co-founder and long-time GTA writer Dan Houser - who's no longer at Rockstar - discussed why the series always seemed to return to America. He said it was because cities like Miami and New York and Los Angeles are places where extreme juxtapositions exist. They're places where extreme wealth rubs shoulders with extreme poverty, and where organised crime can be found.

    There's also something America infamously has that few other countries do, and that's free availability of guns, which is such a core tenet of a GTA experience.

    Sources indicate that nevertheless, Obbe Vermeij - a former technical director at Rockstar North - revealed last year that a GTA: Tokyo almost happened. However, it wasn't going to be made by Rockstar but rather an external team in Japan.

    In a recent development, while discussing the subject, Vermeij referred to America as "basically the epicenter of Western culture". "Everybody knows the cities, even people who haven't been there," Vermeij said. "They have a mental image of the cities. I'm afraid we're stuck in this loop of about five American cities. Let's just get used to it.".

    GTA 6 is just days away from its 19th November release on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. Rockstar recently clarified the game runs at 30FPS across all platforms and confirmed that while it's available through Xbox Cloud Gaming, it cannot be streamed to PCs or non-Xbox devices.

    GTA 6 has already outgrossed the entire box office run of Avengers: Endgame, the highest-grossing movie in history — and the sheer scale of that success is represented in the launch day stats.

    According to Mat Piscatella, senior director and video game industry advisor at Circana, over 50% of all active consoler customers played GTA 6 at launch, averaging 494–513 minutes of playtime, or roughly 8 hours.

    That does not mean 50% of all console consumers played it.

    Recent findings suggest that "For players active on November 19th, 61% of US PlayStation 5 and 56% of global Xbox players engaged with Grand Theft Auto 6," he posted to Bluesky. "PS5 GTA 6 players averaged 513 minutes that day, Xbox players 494. Both the DAU and minutes played engagement rates are absolutely bonkers.".

    Piscatella doesn't have the exact stats to hand, explaining that it's "not exactly easy to go back and sort daily active engagement rates," but to his recollection, during his time at Circana, there has been "nothing near this.".

    It has been revealed that the only game second to GTA 6 on launch was Fortnite, accounting for 10% of all active players across both platforms. Clearly, the Pirate Shop Access tokens are working.

    As for what GTA 6 players were up to before the game debuted, Piscatella had some additional stats, sharing the top-five games between November 6 and 19:.

    $3.7 billion in revenue within 24 hours, "the biggest entertainment launch of all time," accounting for over 50% of all active console users — those numbers are nothing to scoff at.

    In fact, in less than a week, with 32.5 million copies sold, GTA 6 is already one of the best-selling games of all-time. It currently sits on the edge of the top 30 after overtaking Super Mario Odyssey, Borderlands 2, and Monster Hunter: World.

    Considering that GTA 5 is the third best-selling game of all-time, behind only Minecraft and Tetris (clearly, the secret to selling hundreds of millions of copies is blocks), it's easy to imagine GTA 6 landing somewhere near the top.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that as the The Sims 4 continues into its second decade, the volume of new content, major expansions, and long-awaited features has grown in lockstep.
    • The effort required to fix them is what led developer Maxis to make a commitment to improve the game’s technical state, and the developer has now returned to update the community on what to expect in 2026.
    • Recent findings suggest that the quality of life pledge was made in September last year, through the introduction of a roadmap.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that as the The Sims 4 continues into its second decade, the volume of new content, major expansions, and long-awaited features has grown in lockstep. Unfortunately, that has also meant that, given how old the game is, a few technical problems remain a nuisance.

    The effort required to fix them is what led developer Maxis to make a commitment to improve the game’s technical state, and the developer has now returned to update the community on what to expect in 2026.

    Recent findings suggest that the quality of life pledge was made in September last year, through the introduction of a roadmap. Since then, the developer issued one update on its progress. Which brings us to this week’s new blog post, which further builds on everything that’s come before.

    In the post, Maxis revealed a few key areas it’s going to be focusing on going forward. Though specific release dates for these changes were not shared, the list of issues should resonate with many players, as it covers many often-discussed topics.

    Sources indicate that the first stage of the new roadmap covers March through August. Over that period, you can expect Sims' autonomy to improve. This goes for things like how they choose locations for certain actions, they way they interact with certain objects, and even how often they interrupt conversations.

    In a recent development, the infant and caregiver relationship is being updated, too, in order to improve autonomy and make sure your little Sims don’t miss out on milestones and interactions. That stage of the roadmap also includes fixes for black photo problems, and other crashes and freezing.

    The next period takes place September through December, and it includes more interesting changes. One of the goals with this one is to improve Sims’ dining experience, which covers issues around eating and drinking.

    Sources indicate that another important area of focus with this stage is family trees, and relationships between members of the same family. Maxis wants to improve the game’s genealogy systems to make relationship tracking across generations more robust so that your family history isn’t lost.

    Depending on how the first stage goes, you might see more challenges join the list of what the developer is looking at for the second stage of the roadmap.

    The good news is that you won’t have to wait too long for the game’s next patch. Due out in March, this next patch will feature around 55 fixes, including for some commonly reported issues.

    Until then, you may want to check out The Sims 4’s Lost Legacies Event, which is available now until the middle of March. If you picked up the game’s latest expansion, check if you tried those Royalty & Legacy cheats.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that paradox Interactive's Frederik Wester has announced he's stepping down from the role of CEO after a combined decade and a half leading the manufacturer.
    • In a statement announcing the change in leadership, Paradox remarked Wester had "decided to step down as CEO to continue focusing on the tech giant's long-term development as a member of the Board." Paradox's current deputy CEO, Mattias Lilja, will take over Wester's role from 4th January 2027.
    • Sources indicate that "I'm truly grateful to all our engaged players and talented colleagues who contribute to outstanding gaming experiences every day," Wester said of his decision.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that paradox Interactive's Frederik Wester has announced he's stepping down from the role of CEO after a combined decade and a half leading the manufacturer. The news follows several tumultuous years for the publisher best known for grand strategy games including Stellaris, Europa Universalis, and Crusader Kings 3.

    In a statement announcing the change in leadership, Paradox remarked Wester had "decided to step down as CEO to continue focusing on the tech giant's long-term development as a member of the Board." Paradox's current deputy CEO, Mattias Lilja, will take over Wester's role from 4th January 2027. Wester is to remain in the position until then in order "to ensure an orderly transition".

    Sources indicate that "I'm truly grateful to all our engaged players and talented colleagues who contribute to outstanding gaming experiences every day," Wester said of his decision. "They are the ones who made these years amazing. My plan was never to be CEO for life. The goal was to build the foundation before passing the baton on for the next chapter in the firm's journey. Since I returned as CEO, we've streamlined our strategy, rebuilt our pipeline and developed our commercial offering. Mattias has had a central role in laying this foundation, and now is the right time to hand over. Given his experience and vision, he is exceptionally well positioned to take the company to its next level.".

    Wester has twice served as Paradox CEO since joining the company in 2003. His first stint ran from 2009 to 2018, after which he became Paradox's executive chairman of the board. He returned to the CEO role in 2021, and has overseen a troubled period for the company. This has included the embattled development of Vampire: The Masquerade Bloodlines 2 - which finally debuted last October after multiple delays, near cancellation, and a switch in developer. Unfortunately the game failed to resonate with critics and audiences, and Paradox unveiled a 162 percent decline in operating profit earlier this year as a result of its commercial failure.

    In a recent development, wester's most recent watch - which began with an admittance of "inappropriate behaviour" amid a damning report into Paradox's workplace culture - has also seen the high-profile cancellation of Sims competitor Life By You, an indefinite delay for Prison Architect 2 after Paradox parted ways with original developer Double Eleven, and a split with BattleTech studio Harebrained Schemes following the commercial failure of The Lamplighters League. Paradox's Cities Skylines 2 has also been blighted with controversy: after a disastrous launch in 2023, its console release is still yet to emerge, and development is now being handled by a newly introduced studio after Paradox split with former developer Colossal Order last year. In 2004, Wester admitted the publisher had "made the wrong calls in several projects".

    Industry observers note that despite all this, incoming CEO Mattias Lilja remains buoyant. "Paradox has a unique DNA that has made us one of the greats in deep and engaging strategy and management games," he wrote in a statement announcing his promotion. "Now we’re stepping up the pace: we will make further investments in our core business, push the boundaries of our game design, work even more closely with our loyal players, develop more and better tools and services that benefit both modders and players, and continue to sharpen our ways of working and our organisation, with player value in focus.".

    Sources indicate that paradox, does of course, have some promising games on its upcoming slate. Alongside continued work on grand strategy stalwarts like Crusader Kings 3, Europa Universalis 5, and Stellaris, next year sees the release of Lego Skylines, and post-apocalyptic grand strategy game Afterworld is also on the way.

    #109292. Latest Update: GTA 6 Lets You Stop And Even Derail The Train

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (425 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Thegamer ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: GTA 6 Lets You Stop And Even Derail The Train

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (425 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thegamer

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that it might've been impossible, but for 13 years, that didn't stop GTA 5 players from throwing everything they could at the freight train to try and stop it dead in its tracks.
    • Not only can you stop the train in GTA 6, but you can even derail it.
    • Trains are much more dynamic this time around, reacting to their environment rather than pushing on full steam ahead without any thought to what's in front of them.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that it might've been impossible, but for 13 years, that didn't stop GTA 5 players from throwing everything they could at the freight train to try and stop it dead in its tracks. What began with ramming a dump truck into it quickly spiraled into spawning 100 rhino tanks, placing a UFO on the tracks, or even flooding Los Santos with a tsunami. Nothing worked. So, when GTA 6 finally hit store shelves, the number one question people raced to answer was: can you stop the train?

    Not only can you stop the train in GTA 6, but you can even derail it. As shown by Twitter user jax_caine (video embedded below), the train isn't an unstoppable force of nature anymore. Hitting it from the side causes it to swerve off the rails, and if you wait around for another train, the two will collide.

    Trains are much more dynamic this time around, reacting to their environment rather than pushing on full steam ahead without any thought to what's in front of them.

    Industry observers note that if you stand on the tracks, a train will brake before hitting you. Likewise, when the train sees another train blocking the tracks, rather than ramming into it at full speed and causing a massive pile-up, it'll slow down. Hell, if you put a body on the tracks, they stop and even sound their horn at you.

    In a recent development, GTA 5's trains worked a little differently. They're static objects and their position is updated through coordinates, independent of physics interactions, which means that instead of reacting to the game's physics engine, they follow hard-coded tracks and override anything in their way. That's why they turn into submersibles when you flood Los Santos, and easily tear through 100 tanks. They literally can't be stopped.

    Recent findings suggest that we don't know exactly how they work in GTA 6 yet, but it's clear they aren't static objects anymore. They behave like other vehicles, reacting dynamically to the world. You could fly a plane into the train and it'd be thrown off course, rather than bravely continuing ahead without a scratch.

    It has been revealed that still, even with GTA 6 in hand and a train that we can derail, I doubt that'll stop the community from finding increasingly elaborate ways to stop the freight train. Even if they never do. With that mystery out of the way, maybe we can turn our attention to those strange symbols near Manifest Canyon, eh?

    • The latter, meanwhile, worked on the excellent Assassin's Creed Shadows and also developed the underrated Switch gem Immortals Fenyx Rising.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Ubisoft has confirmed that it is laying off a total of 166 members of staff from its Canadian offices.

    The teams affected, Ubisoft Montréal and Ubisoft Québec, are arguably two of the most prominent studios in the corporation. The former has been responsible for some of the most well-regarded entries in the Assassin's Creed series along with key entries in the Far Cry franchise.

    The latter, meanwhile, worked on the excellent Assassin's Creed Shadows and also developed the underrated Switch gem Immortals Fenyx Rising.

    GamesIndustry.biz states that the layoffs account for less than 4% of the total workforce at the studios, and that the employees affected were working on projects that had either been cancelled or significantly changed.

    Here's the statement provided by Ubisoft:.

    "Ubisoft is reducing its workforce by 166 positions across its Montréal and Québec City operations. As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.

    It has been revealed that "We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognise the impact this may have on our colleagues. We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect. Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources.".

    Ubisoft's next major release is Rayman Legends Retold, a reimagined remake of the 2013 classic Rayman Legends, developed in collaboration by Ubisoft Milan and Montpellier.

    Industry observers note that what do you make of this latest round of layoffs from Ubisoft? Share a comment in the usual place and let us know.

    To pass time and skip ahead in GTA 6 is something that will become more and more of a priority as you progress through the game, with certain quests and activities being tied to certain points in the day or night. That means that if you want to do a night time mission and it's early in the morning, you can either wait for that time to pass, or you can find a way to skip ahead to the moment you need. Below I'll show you how to do that in GTA 6, and the limitations on this system overall.

    To pass time in GTA 6 and skip ahead, the best way to do this is to go to bed. When you lie down and choose to sleep, you also get to pick what time your character wakes up, setting your alarm for morning, noon, evening or night accordingly.

    Obviously this means getting back to your home, which for some might easier than others, depending on where you are. You should also make sure that you don't have any time-sensitive missions or activities (marked with an hourglass). If you do, you risk sleeping through them and missing the chance to engage with them. Make sure you check through the GTA 6 index to see if there's anything that's being put at risk.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.
    • HoYoverse announced last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020.
    • Sources indicate that the game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.

    HoYoverse announced last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020. And with Version Luna 5, those end days are upon us.

    Sources indicate that the game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed. But as of today, paid purchases from the in-game store have been disabled on PS4; and in six weeks' time, on approximately April 8, Version Luna 6 will discontinue access to the PS4 version altogether.

    In many ways this is unsurprising – Genshin is already available on both PS5 and Xbox Series to sate fans eager to play on console, and the PS4's hardware is increasingly struggling to keep up with this massive open-world game after more than five years of regular updates have ballooned both its file size and technical requirements.

    It has been revealed that aptly enough, Luna 5 takes the main story action back to the nation of Mondstadt, the location where the Traveler (and, by extension, the players) took their first steps into the world of Teyvat back in September 2020. It feels like a symbolic last hurrah for the original console home of the game, as does the inclusion of a Chronicled Wish banner focussing on some of Mondstadt's most iconic (read: too old to be meta by now) 5-Star characters – namely Eula, Mona, Albedo, Klee, Diluc, and Jean.

    And as the icing on the Tea Break Pancake, this banner is running alongside the long-anticipated introduction of Varka – the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius who has been a major character in the game's lore from the very beginning, but who only became playable with today's upgrade.

    Looking ahead to that post-Luna 6 future, Genshin Impact will still be available on PS5, as well as Xbox Series consoles, PC, and mobile devices – so hopefully anyone who is still playing primarily on PS4 will find another platform they can continue the adventure on by April.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Developer FromSoftware has confirmed that online multiplayer servers for Dark Souls 2 and 3 are back online following a nearly two-week outage.
    • It has been revealed that fromSoftware temporarily disabled multiplayer on 30th October, citing what it called "a server glitch".
    • FromSoftware never specified the exact concern impacting its servers, and today's statement is equally vague.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Developer FromSoftware has confirmed that online multiplayer servers for Dark Souls 2 and 3 are back online following a nearly two-week outage.

    It has been revealed that fromSoftware temporarily disabled multiplayer on 30th October, citing what it called "a server glitch". Some speculated this could be related to the recently discovered PHP security bug, which impacted a number of other games.

    FromSoftware never specified the exact concern impacting its servers, and today's statement is equally vague. "Regarding the temporary suspension of the game server for Dark Souls 2, and Dark Souls 3, the investigation has been completed and the fix has been applied. The game server and online features are now restored," a notice on Dark Souls' official site reads.

    "We sincerely apologise for the inconvenience caused, and thank you for your patience and understanding.".

    Online servers do more in FromSoftware games than simply facilitating co-op and PvP; they're also responsible for handling messages players leave for each other in-game, as well as the ghostly representations of players who just went through the same area, helping the Dark Souls series' forlorn worlds feel a little less solitary.

    Recent findings suggest that this isn't the first time Dark Souls servers have gone offline, either. In 2022, servers for all three games went offline due to a vulnerability that allowed malicious code to run on them. In that instance, it took FromSoftware three months to bring servers back online for some games, and as many as nine months for others.

    In other FromSoftware news, the studio recently confirmed - following months of speculation - it's officially delaying the Switch 2-exclusive The Duskbloods to sometime in 2027.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love.
    • As is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year.
    • Industry observers note that the standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love. Today, we learned the list of nominees for the 2027 Grammy ceremony, and it's an interesting lineup. The nominations are as follows:.

    As is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year. On that note, it's most surprising to see that Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora has been nominated for the third year in a row: once for the base game, once for the Secrets of the Spires DLC, and now for the From The Ashes DLC. None of these soundtracks are bad by any means, but their Grammy representation far outweighs their cultural footprint.

    Industry observers note that the standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into. However, it's also a Sony-published game, which have a pretty good track record of getting nominations, potentially due to the company's massive presence in the music and film industries. Still, Ghost of Yōtei has a great, unique score that's deserving of its spot, and also one previously nominated for best music at the 2025 Game Awards. The Grammys accept any releases between October 1 of one year and September 30 of the following year, so Ghost of Yōtei barely made the cut for this window. The Game Awards nominees will be revealed tomorrow – it will be interesting to see how much overlap there is between the categories.

    In a recent development, this batch of Grammy noms also has fewer recurring nominees than past years. This is Gordy Haab's third nomination (he won in 2024 for Star Wars Jedi: Survivor) and John Paesano's second nomination (he was nominated in 2025 for Marvel's Spider-Man 2). It's also the first year since the awards' creation without Bear McCreary or Austin Wintory nominations.

    Last year's nominations left a sour taste in the mouths of many, with several DLC nominees and a complete lack of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, the year's standout hit that many specifically praised for its music. This year certainly has snubs (Mewgenics, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and Control Resonant all come to mind), but none as egregious as last year.

    What do you think was the best video game score from the last year? Let us know in the comments!

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that microsoft 365 isn't quite living up to its name this week, as its services have suffered an extended outage that's knocked the likes of Outlook, Teams, and Copilot for six. As of writing, the tech giant are finally reporting "encouraging recovery progress in Europe" and are busy "addressing the remaining areas of disruption", but that's only after chunks of November 12th and 13th have seen people, businesses, and institutions left unable to use stuff they rely on.

    In a recent development, that latest upgrade was given by Microsoft to the BBC, who've had a live report on the outage running, since it's affected the likes of schools, government services and medical services. IGN and Kotaku's reports differ on whether any Xbox services appear to be affected. The Xbox status support page at the moment indicates all is swell, but Downdetector does show a recent uptick in reports of challenges.

    According to recent reports, "We regret that today’s outages caused disruptions for our customers, and we are working to address the issue," Microsoft exec Charles LaManna wrote in response to a support thread on the topic in the early hours of November 13th UK time. "We will continue to share more information as soon as we have it, and for now I can confirm that there is no indication this is the result of malicious or cyber activity.".

    As much as it's slightly reassuring that there at the moment looks to have been no significant hack, the time it's taken to deploy proper fixes is concerning, with Microsoft noting some of their early attempts at rectifying things "not taking as expected".

    According to recent reports, the debacle has rather emphasised how far from ideal it is that so much key infrastructure across the world runs on one clump of tech which all go down in a heartbeat, but to a certain degree that is the peril of relying on anything. One can only hope that Microsoft's ongoing efforts to fire vast numbers of staff into the sun and embrace AI haven't factored into lots of their services going tits up for an inconvenient amount of time.

    It seems like we’re getting one of these every few months, but the world of mobile action RPGs that look like the games that, just a few years back, were only possible on consoles is expanding with another latest entry.

    Netmarble, a studio and publisher known for its free-to-play games on mobile and PC, recently unveiled the launch date for The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin, its next major release that’s very much coming for the Genshin Impact crowd.

    The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin is an open-world action RPG based on the world of The Seven Deadly Sins anime and manga. The game takes place in the world of Britannia, which looks similar to the way it does in the anime.

    Sources indicate that that said, the story of the game is not based on the anime or manga, Instead, it’s an original story set in the universe of the show. You play as Prince Tristan of the Kingdom of Liones who must find a way to bring order back to Britannia.

    The gameplay should be familiar to anyone who played a free-to-play action RPG in the last decade. It features action combat, a roster of diverse heroes that you assemble to form teams, and a large pretty world to explore where you’ll also get to meet fresh characters.

    Recent findings suggest that speaking of which, while Origin has its own original story, expect to be teaming up with characters from the series - some of whom wouldn't be able to meet naturally. You can thank the game's multiversal story for that.

    In a recent development, beyond all the serious business of saving the world and battling monsters, The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin also has a cozy, relaxing side. You’ll be able to fish, cook, forage and take on the beauty of the world with your pals.

    The game has a bit of an unusual release schedule. It’s set to arrive on PC, PS5, iOS, and Android. PC (Steam), and PS5 players will be able to jump in starting March 16, whereas the global mobile launch is scheduled for one week later, on March 23.

    You can pre-register right now on the official website if you’re interested in earning a few rewards when the game introduces. You can, of course, always wishlist the game on Steam and the PlayStation Store, too.

    Latest Update: Feature: 10 Features That Surprised Me While Playing GTA 6 On Xbox Series X

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By now, you've hopefully had a chance to check out our review of GTA 6 for Xbox Series X elsewhere on Pure Xbox, and it exists because Rockstar gave us multiple weeks' worth of early access to the game ahead of release.
    • I was the lucky person to take on the review responsibility for the new Grand Theft Auto, and I've put basically all of my free time into it since late October.
    • Some of these were already known prior to today, whereas others might be brand-new information.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By now, you've hopefully had a chance to check out our review of GTA 6 for Xbox Series X elsewhere on Pure Xbox, and it exists because Rockstar gave us multiple weeks' worth of early access to the game ahead of release.

    I was the lucky person to take on the review responsibility for the new Grand Theft Auto, and I've put basically all of my free time into it since late October. While completing the campaign, I inevitibly came across loads of features that surprised me along the way, so I thought I'd use this opportunity to just highlight a few of them.

    Some of these were already known prior to today, whereas others might be brand-new information. In any case, here are the specific features (avoiding story spoilers) that surprised me as I was completing GTA 6 on Xbox Series X:.

    According to recent reports, yeah, there's finally a fuel requirement in a GTA game! It's not too invasive, so don't worry, but if you happen to drive a car around the map for an extensive amount of time, you'll be forced to find a gas station and refuel it (a very short cutscene and a press of the RT button). You can also repair your car at gas stations as well, which certainly comes in handy if you've been smashing it around at high speeds!

    Industry observers note that you can still break into vehicles the old fashioned way - either stealing it mid-drive or smashing a window to gain access - but you can also use a slim-jim to break the lock, or eventually a key cloner to bypass the security entirely. Be aware of vehicles with trackers though, as if you end up going too slow, the tracker will alert the cops to your location.

    Recent findings suggest that it's not always enough to escape the cops and stay hidden from them for an extended period of time. If you really want to ensure you'll lose their attention, you'll want to either ditch the car or take it to a "Pay 'n' Spray" outlet, as well as change your outfit. It's possible to partially do this by throwing on some sunglasses and a hat, but the clever move is to stash one or more outfits in your car's trunk that you can switch between at a moment's notice.

    While it's impossible to avoid situations in GTA 6 where you'll be engaging in all sorts of criminal activity, you can handle them in various ways. For example, a mission that requires you to take out a bunch of people can be completed by one-shotting them all, but this will raise your criminal profile. Alternatively, leaving your enemies injured but still alive will push you more towards a "Professional" profile. I haven't properly been able to compare how this affects the game yet (I really need to experiment with both sides of the extreme rather than hovering towards the middle), but Rockstar notes it alters how the story, world and Jason / Lucia react to you.

    In a recent development, I always love when games get creative with music - South of Midnight was one that really impressed me - and GTA 6 is now one of the best examples I can think of. Basically, you get highly-curated pumping tunes playing in the background during things like shootouts and getaways, while more menacing situations can feature a different vibe of soundtrack, sometimes even with lyrics. You might not quite understand the appeal until you play it, but it's actually one of my favourite latest features. The use of music in certain cutscenes is awesome as well.

    According to recent reports, I don't know if I can verify this yet for sure, but the radio stations either appear to change their music selection based on where you are on the map, or based on how far you've progressed into the story. As I spent more time in Vice City, I started to notice a much bigger range of songs on the Flash FM channel (my favourite) including everyone from Coldplay to The Ting Tings, whereas those tunes never popped up at the start. Try it for yourself and let me know if I'm right about this!

    Any GTA game worth its salt has to come with a whole bunch of minigames, and my favourite so far is the addition of minigolf. I believe there are three 18-hole courses dotted around the map in total, and they're beautifully detailed and themed, with genuinely enjoyable holes to play on. There's actual golf as well, but I have to admit I haven't had chance to check it out yet. Pool in the bars is great fun too!

    In a recent development, if you really take your time to play through GTA 6, which I highly recommend you do, you'll truly be able to appreciate just how much effort has gone into some of the seemingly smallest aspects of it. Snapmatic, which is the social media platform on your in-game phone, is constantly being updated with upcoming statuses, photos, videos, comments and more, and you could literally just sit just browsing it for ages and enjoying the interactions. There's also a "News" app that regularly gets updated with fresh articles about what's going on in Leonida.

    Industry observers note that when you get to a certain mission in GTA 6, you'll be introduced to your first video game inside the game itself, which seems to be a very high-brow parody of modern-day indie hits. There are actually multiple games you can play, including one that's very reminiscent of Xbox title Yet Another Zombie Survivors, and these can either be accessed by turning on your TV or going up to arcade cabinets located in various stores all over the map.

    When GTA 5 came out for Xbox 360 back in 2013, one of the significant things I can recall is how slow the initial loading screens would be, especially once GTA Online got involved. We obviously haven't got an online component to GTA 6 just yet, but in terms of loading up the single-player game on Xbox Series X, it's actually a very quick process that isn't painful whatsoever. You barely even notice it!

    Sources indicate that of course, these aren't the only surprising features you'll run into while playing GTA 6 - there are literally hundreds and hundreds that are waiting to be discovered. I don't want to spoil anything about the story or the details of the missions themselves though, and ultimately this is a game where surprises will continue being revealed long into the future.

    For now, just go and enjoy it on your Xbox Series X or Xbox Series S (or PS5), and I urge you to take your time and really let it all soak in. One of the perils of reviewing games is that you have to grind to the finish line, and while that does still give you a great impression of the experience, I already can't wait to go back and spend 100+ hours with it this time.

    Anything here sound particularly enticing to you? Let us know down in the comments section below.

    The Witcher 3 uses gen-AI to enhance Geralt's Polish voice following actor's stroke - "I do think this is one of those ways where you can use AI ethically"

    📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (597 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • CD Projekt Red has revealed that it used - and is using - generative AI technology to treat and alter the voice of the Polish actor who portrayed Geralt of Rivia in upcoming Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past.
    • The actor, Jacek Rozenek, has portrayed Geralt of Rivia in all the major Witcher games, meaning his voice has become as synonymous with the role in Poland as Doug Cockle's has for people playing in English.
    • It's for these reasons that CD Projekt Red - with Rozenek's consent - employed the help of a manufacturer called Respeecher to alter the lines he recorded for The Witcher 3's Songs of the Past expansion using generative-AI technology.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    CD Projekt Red has revealed that it used - and is using - generative AI technology to treat and alter the voice of the Polish actor who portrayed Geralt of Rivia in upcoming Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past.

    The actor, Jacek Rozenek, has portrayed Geralt of Rivia in all the major Witcher games, meaning his voice has become as synonymous with the role in Poland as Doug Cockle's has for people playing in English. But Rozenek suffered a severe stroke in 2019 that left him temporarily unable to speak, and when he was able to talk and perform again, the tonality and quality of his voice had changed.

    It's for these reasons that CD Projekt Red - with Rozenek's consent - employed the help of a manufacturer called Respeecher to alter the lines he recorded for The Witcher 3's Songs of the Past expansion using generative-AI technology. As confirmed to Game File, an AI trained on Rozenek's previous Witcher work is retreating his recordings to make them sound more like the Geralt you hear elsewhere in The Witcher 3.

    Sources indicate that "The point is that this voice should be as close as possible to my voice from 12 years ago," Jacek Rozenek explained. "I have great trust ... for the creators of this game.".

    It has been revealed that game File heard both treated and untreated recordings of Rozenek's Songs of the Past work, and reported a "significant" difference between them. Rozenek's untreated voice was apparently "deep and gravelly" and "noticeably rougher than his recordings for the original game". But treated, the voice was "far smoother and sounds younger", and closer to the original Witcher 3 Geralt recordings.

    According to recent reports, this isn't the first time CD Projekt Red has used generative AI for voice recordings in one of its games. The studio worked with Respeecher in 2023 to produce new voiceover lines for Cyberpunk 2077 expansion Phantom Liberty. Viktor Vektor actor Miłogost "Miłek" Reczek passed away in 2021, after the original game was released, and CD Projekt Red didn't want to recast the role. Reczek's sons apparently gave their blessing for their father's voice to be artificially generated.

    "I do think this is one of those ways where you can use AI ethically with consent and also to do something good," CD Projekt Red localisation producer Mikołaj Szwed told Game File, referring to the Rozenek recordings.

    "For future projects, when we consider Geralt is becoming older and has a deeper voice, this is not a problem for us at all. It's more about this specific situation here, where we have both the voice from 12 years ago and from now next to each other, which could kind of take people out of the experience and feel that there is this difference.".

    Recent findings suggest that the third Witcher 3 expansion, Songs of the Past, releases at some point next year, an unprecedented 12 years after the original game launched. It adds an entirely new region, Letten, and centres its main story around Geralt's missing bardic bestie Dandelion, whose family lives there.

    In preparation for the expansion, a remastered version of The Witcher 3 was released a couple of months ago, overhauling the old role-playing adventure and bringing its baseline presentation more in line with what we'd expect from a modern game; it also overhauled some animations and enemy behaviours and reworked skill trees. For that reason, old-gen consoles PS4 and Xbox One won't receive the Songs of the Past expansion, despite The Witcher 3 being available on them.

    #109282. Toy Story 3 Remaster Highlights How Movie Games Should Be Done

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (882 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Thegamer ↗ Open Full Page

    Toy Story 3 Remaster Highlights How Movie Games Should Be Done

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (882 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thegamer

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that toy Story 3 is often regarded as one of the better games based on a movie.
    • Not only bring those games back, but bundle them together.
    • For decades, movie tie-in games were commonplace.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that toy Story 3 is often regarded as one of the better games based on a movie. A legitimately great 3D platformer that also immerses fans of the films in its world in ways that not many other tie-in games have ever managed to pull off. That’s why those of us who played it when it originally released were thrilled to find out it was part of Digital Eclipse’s surprising effort to bring pretty much all past Toy Story games to modern platforms.

    Not only bring those games back, but bundle them together. The Retro Roundup, which combines all of the older games from the ‘90s and early ‘00s into one collection, and a remaster of Toy Story 3 for modern platforms. Best of all, the Roundup and the remaster can be bought as part of the same bundle, not just digitally, but physically, too.

    For decades, movie tie-in games were commonplace. Almost expected, particularly for the bigger Disney blockbusters. Aladdin, Hercules, Tarzan - they all had games that were released alongside their movies, giving fans another way to experience what they had just seen on the significant screen.

    In a recent development, that tradition has all but died out for several reasons. Trying to release a game and a movie at the same time is no longer possible, largely due to how long it takes to make games that would be considered worthy of significant-budget blockbusters. Even if a developer were to hit the ground running the second the mere idea for a movie was uttered, that movie would still end up getting made long before the game was even close to being finished, likely by a margin of years.

    It’s why Toy Story 3 was probably one of the last true movie tie-in games we will ever get, which is somewhat ironic as it’s also one of the best. The trouble is, especially now with the release of its remaster, people are looking back on it and longing for another era where movies can have tie-in games released alongside them. It’s not the feeling of long-lost nostalgia we should be focusing on when playing this remaster, though. Developers and movie studios should be looking at what Disney and Avalanche did with that original game, what Digital Eclipse has done with the remaster, and using all of that as the blueprint for the future of movie games.

    Recent findings suggest that even though the Toy Story 3 game and movie were released at the same time, the former isn’t just a game version of the latter. It’s effectively a love letter to the entire series, or at least the original trilogy, that pulls from those first three beloved movies. Its developers were given more freedom, which is how we wound up with the more open Woody’s Roundup area, one of the - if not the - main reasons the game was so popular.

    It has been revealed that the game didn’t need to release alongside the movie to be a success, something its Complete Edition has now proved 16 years later. Those who played the original have been reminded of just how good it was, and how it told a separate Toy Story story while remaining faithful to the films, and Disney now has a shiny new polished version to point new, younger fans towards not just when a new Toy Story movie is released, but whenever they need to.

    That’s the lesson that other studios which have all-but given up on movie games really need to try and learn from. That you don’t need to pull off the almost-impossible and try to get the launch of a movie and its game to perfectly align. What’s more crucial is making sure that game is good and can stand the test of time. If so, you can not only release it whenever, but whenever you need it again, you have something to point to. Or, if it’s been long enough, you can give it the remaster treatment like Toy Story 3.

    Industry observers note that I wouldn’t even be averse to seeing Toy Story 3 dusted off and remastered a second time a decade from now, perhaps to give Toy Story fans who haven’t even been born yet something to play two console generations from now when the sixth, seventh, and eighth movies are released. Add an extra area to Woody’s Roundup. Throw in a few more story missions. It’s certainly a lot easier than making a whole fresh game from scratch, which is the problem that has effectively ended the movie video game era.

    Recent findings suggest that I appreciate that “Hey, just make a game that’s as good as Toy Story 3 and you’ll be set for life” is easier noted than done. The thing is, I don’t think anyone is even trying. Just look at the excitement surrounding the reveal of the Coco world in Kingdom Hearts 4. There’s a Coco sequel coming, and a game like Toy Story 3 set in that world could be huge, even if it doesn’t line up with the release of its sequel. Sadly, I think Coco’s inclusion in KH is the closest we’ll ever get to a video game set in Disney’s Land of the Dead.
